items.title: Table of contents for markdown panes
items.text: Markdown viewers with two or more headings now get a native contents card that tracks the section you're reading and jumps you to any heading. Wide panes get it in a left gutter with the document reflowing beside it; narrow panes get a slide-in overlay from the navigation bar. It's the same glass card as the pane banner, so it looks like part of the app rather than part of the page.

items.title: Markdown reads like macOS content
items.text: Body text is now set in the system font (SF Pro) and code in SF Mono, with sizing and leading retuned to match, instead of GitHub's web font stack.

items.title: Viewer panes browse like a browser
items.text: Every viewer, files included, now has an editable address bar plus back / forward / reload / home. Type a URL (or just `example.com`) to go to the web, or type a path to point the pane back at a file — and Back crosses that boundary correctly. Home returns to wherever the pane was originally opened, tracked separately from where you've navigated since, and both survive a session restore. `--view=about:blank` (or "Viewer: Open Browser Pane" in the command palette) opens a blank pane with the caret already in the address field.

items.title: IPC commands hit the right app
items.text: Each pane now knows the socket of the app instance that owns it, so `ghoztty +split` run inside a debug-build pane splits the debug window instead of silently driving the release app. Works on every pane kind — plain, session-persistence, and remote — and falls back to the old behavior outside Ghoztty.

items.title: Recovery no longer kills the sessions it recovers
items.text: A brief hiccup on the local agent link could rebuild your windows and then terminate the very sessions it had just re-attached. Recovery now waits to confirm the agent is actually gone before acting, a pane that gets swapped out is no longer mistaken for one you closed, and the agent refuses a shutdown request from a superseded connection.

items.title: Hero mode follows the live layout
items.text: Splits created or closed after entering hero mode are now reachable, and with two windows in hero mode a single keystroke moves only the window you're aiming at instead of stepping both.

items.title: `+split --target=<window>` works with a viewer focused
items.text: It used to exit 0 and do nothing.

items.title: Random window tints are actually distinguishable
items.text: `--color=random` windows stay dark but now lift off pure black, so the hue reads.
